What happens to the relationship when your partner starts “p*nis-maxxing”?
Cosmopolitan reports, “men are paying thousands of dollars to get the p*nis of their dreams.” Sometimes it’s a Glade can, sometimes the results are more modest. But either way, men are opting for the latest maxxing trend without shame, and seemingly, for the most part, without trepidation.But maybe there should be slightly more misgivings around this particular maxxing forefront.“Much of the online conversation is fuelled by unrealistic expectations, misinformation and highly edited portrayals of male bodies, which can create unnecessary anxiety and insecurity,” one aesthetic doctor recently said in an interview.

Sarah Huckabee Sanders casts lazy white guy named Brad in anti-welfare ad & Republicans are pissed
white guy.Stay woke with our briefing while staying informed on all things LGBTQ+ entertainment, life, and more!We’re not joking! The MAGA crowd is angry that the spot portrays a young white guy on Medicaid, opposed to, you know, a person of color.While Sanders speaks, the slovenly dude is lounging in sweats, playing video games and throwing cheese balls and potato chips in his mouth (often missing, The NY Times notes).“Brad has turned relaxing into a full-time profession,” Sanders tells the camera. “But you, you actually work hard. You pay taxes to cover welfare for guys like Brad, who just choose not to work.”You pay taxes to cover welfare for people who just choose not to work.

01.10 / 22:37
Andrew Fuller dishes on living colorfully in these “beige” times, Halloween Wars & the gayest cake he’s ever made
Netflix‘s Is It Cake?, and certainly not now that he’s a judge on Food Network’s seasonal baking competition series Halloween Wars.Subscribe to our newsletter for a refreshing cocktail (or mocktail) of LGBTQ+ entertainment and pop culture, served up with a side of eye-candy.“We’re living in dark times—actually, maybe they’re more like beige times,” he tells Queerty, “where everybody is expected to look like everybody else and take themselves way too seriously.” So he knows that expressing his individuality on national television means he can be an important beacon of hope for all the other “young weirdos and queerdos” out there.That also makes him uniquely suited to judge Halloween Wars, a show that challenges cake artists to be their weirdest selves. Alongside host Jonathan Bennett and fellow judge Shinmin Li, Fuller says being welcomed into this celebration of all things ooky-spooky has been a real treat, even if being on the other side of a baking competition series comes with challenges of its own: “The biggest trick was realizing how emotionally connected I would become to every team and the work they were putting in,” he reveals.So, with October finally upon us and another batch of Halloween Wars in full-swing, we thought it was the perfect time to invite Fuller into the hot seat for our long-running Q&A series Dishin’ It.
01.10 / 22:01
Grindr drops of a whopping $250 million on its next big venture
Grindr has announced its first major acquisition of another company. Yesterday, in a statement to investors, it revealed it was preparing to pay $250 million for the online PrEP clinic Freddie.Freddie is an LGBTQ+-focused digital health clinic specializing in barrier-free PrEP access. It was founded in Canada in 2020 and then expanded into the US in 2024.The purchase is undoubtedly part of Grindr’s efforts to be seen as more than just a dating app.

Hot for hockey? NHL tries to jump on the Heated Rivalry bandwagon… but forgets the most important part
Heated Rivalry, the NHL is using the steamy hockey romance as a blueprint on how to better markets its own versions of Ilya Rozanov and Shane Hollander. Except they’re leaving out a vital part. With a new season starting this week, the NHL unveiled its “Hot for Hockey” campaign.
